evidence.note: Opening prose states intent to pin the contract first and identifies the broad subsystem slice (engine, spills, collab, csv/xlsx, validation, formatting, pivots, locale) — foundational-first instinct, but no explicit ordered milestone plan with per-item done-criteria is written.

Architectural sequencing (launcher before app, JSON store, persist-per-mutation) but the entire app across all ~15 subsystems was written in a single monolithic 63KB apply_patch rather than built as sequenced milestones.

Verification run in chunks with a sensible foundational-first ordering: api/engine/deps first, then spills/copy/sort/csv, then xlsx/ooxml/iter/pivot/locale/validation — rough milestones tied to getting dev_tests chunks green.

Foundational recompute/aggregate correctness bugs (INDEX, SUM flattening) surfaced only after the whole app was built, showing build-all-then-fix rather than nailing foundational correctness before layering features.
Full suite green plus an explicit manual persistence-restart done-check (create workbook, write formula, stop/start, re-read B1=42) — a concrete verification hook for the persistence milestone.

reasoning: The agent showed a sensible foundational-first orientation and used concrete done-checks (health endpoint, chunked test passes ordered core→dependent, an explicit persistence restart check), which exceeds a flat unordered to-do list (anchor 3). But it never produced an explicit dependency-aware milestone decomposition of the ~15 subsystems; instead it built everything in one monolithic patch and discovered foundational dependency/aggregate bugs only afterward, so it did not 'nail foundational correctness before layering' as anchor 8 requires. The ordering that exists is mostly in verification chunks tied to dev_tests going green, matching anchor 5 with a slight lean toward 6 for the concrete verification hooks.
